questions.stem: What is the approximate percentage of nitrogen in the Earth's atmosphere today?
questions.explanation: The Earth's atmosphere is approximately 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen, about 1% argon, and 0.04% carbon dioxide, with trace amounts of other gases.

questions.stem: What were the main gases in the Earth's early atmosphere (about 4.6 billion years ago)?
questions.explanation: The early atmosphere was mainly carbon dioxide and water vapour, released by intense volcanic activity. It was similar to the atmospheres of Mars and Venus today.

questions.stem: How did the oceans form on Earth?

options.text: Ice caps melted due to volcanic activity
Water was brought by comets from space
The water vapour in the atmosphere condensed as the Earth cooled

questions.explanation: As the Earth gradually cooled, the water vapour in the early atmosphere condensed to form the oceans. This was a key step in the evolution of the atmosphere.

questions.stem: How was most of the carbon dioxide removed from the early atmosphere?

options.text: It dissolved in the oceans and was locked up in sedimentary rocks and fossil fuels
It was absorbed by animals through breathing
It was destroyed by ultraviolet radiation

questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide dissolved in the oceans, was used by marine organisms to make shells (forming limestone), and was taken in by plants for photosynthesis. Over millions of years, it became locked in sedimentary rocks and fossil fuels.

questions.stem: Which organisms were responsible for producing the oxygen in the atmosphere?
questions.explanation: Early algae and plants produced oxygen through photosynthesis. Over billions of years, oxygen levels gradually increased to the 21% we have today.

questions.stem: Which gas makes up about 0.04% of the current atmosphere and is important for plant growth?
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide makes up about 0.04% of the atmosphere. Although a small proportion, it is essential for photosynthesis and plays a significant role as a greenhouse gas.

questions.stem: Why has the proportion of nitrogen in the atmosphere remained relatively stable over time?

options.text: Nitrogen is unreactive, so it is not easily removed from the atmosphere
Nitrogen is very reactive and quickly replenished
Nitrogen is constantly produced by volcanoes

questions.explanation: Nitrogen is a very unreactive gas, so once it accumulated in the atmosphere it was not easily removed by chemical reactions. This is why it has remained the most abundant gas.
